title: Benchmarking Prompt Optimization of Large Language Models With Chess
abstract: arXiv:2610.00416v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Evaluating large language models becomes increasingly challenging as their capabilities advance: benchmarks can saturate, public test sets risk contamination, and assessing harder tasks can require expensive grading or execution infrastructure. These challenges are amplified in automatic prompt optimization (APO), where evaluation is repeated throughout the search for better prompts. Studying APO therefore requires a benchmark that is cheap and deterministic to score, hard enough to leave room for improvement, and renewable as models evolve. We introduce a chess benchmark built from 1,118 Lichess puzzles to study APO for frozen LLMs: we optimize their prompts without updating their model weights. Chess combines inexpensive exact-match scoring, engine-based evaluation of alternative moves, and a renewable supply of problems with adjustable difficulty. translated_title: 基于国际象棋的大语言模型提示词优化基准测试
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型能力的不断提升，对其评估变得越来越具有挑战性：基准测试可能饱和，公开测试集面临数据污染的风险，而评估更难的任务可能需要昂贵的评分或执行基础设施。这些挑战在自动提示词优化（APO）中被进一步放大，因为在搜索更优提示词的过程中需要反复进行评估。因此，研究APO需要一个评分成本低且结果确定、难度足够高以留出改进空间、并随模型演进可持续更新的基准测试。我们引入了一个由1,118道Lichess棋题构建的国际象棋基准测试，用于研究冻结大语言模型（即不更新模型权重、仅优化提示词）的自动提示词优化。国际象棋结合了低成本的精确匹配评分、基于引擎的备选着法评估，以及难度可调且可持续更新的题源。与仅报告孤立测试项成功率的评估不同，该基准测试还……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于1,118道Lichess国际象棋棋题的基准测试，利用国际象棋低成本精确评分、引擎辅助着法评估和可持续更新的可调难度题源等特性，来研究冻结大语言模型的自动提示词优化。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a chess benchmark built from 1,118 Lichess puzzles that leverages cheap exact-match scoring, engine-based move evaluation, and a renewable supply of adjustable-difficulty problems to study automatic prompt optimization (APO) for frozen LLMs.
